newsitem.title: NEPAL: German president to tour Nepal next week.
newsitem.headline: German president to tour Nepal next week.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog will visit Nepal next week, the first foreign head of state to tour the Himalayan kingdom since the establishment of multi-party democracy six years ago, the Foreign Ministry said.
The ministry said on Tuesday that Herzog and his wife, Christiane, would arrive in the capital Kathmandu on a state visit on November 25 as guests of King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya.
King Birendra, the world's only Hindu monarch, will host a state banquet in honour of the German leader, who will visit three ancient towns studded with old pagoda temples in the Kathmandu valley.

Herzog will hold talks with Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba and also tour the pictursque town of Pokhara, famous among Western tourists for its panoramic view of legendary Fishtail mountain in west Nepal.
Germany is one of Nepal's leading donors.
One of the 10 poorest countries of the world, the kingdom depends on foreign aid to fund more than 60 percent of its economic development.

Bonn is the largest buyer of Nepal's hand-knotted woollen carpets. In the 1995/96 fiscal year ended in mid-July, Germany purchased $113.6 million worth of rugs, more than 80 percent of the kingdom's total carpet exports.
A German delegation recently said bilateral aid would increase to $28 million this year from $20 million in 1995.

Several foreign heads of government have visited Nepal since bloody demonstrations forced King Birendra to restore multi-party democracy six years ago, but Herzog would be the first president or monarch.
